'''Alexander Givental''' ({{langx|ru|Александр Борисович Гивенталь}}<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mathnet.ru/php/person.phtml?personid=21886&option_lang=rus|title=	Гивенталь Александр Борисович|access-date=August 5, 2011}}</ref>) is a Russian-American mathematician who is currently Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].  His main contributions have been in [[symplectic topology]] and [[singularity theory]], as well as their relation to topological string theories.

==Education==
Givental graduated from the famed Moscow high school No. 2 ({{interlanguage link|Лицей «Вторая школа»|ru}}), one of the math teachers was [[Valery Senderov]], but was not able to enter a program at a top university due to [[antisemitism in Soviet mathematics]]. He completed his undergraduate and master studies at the [[Gubkin Russian State University of Oil and Gas]], and defended his PhD under the supervision of [[V. I. Arnold]] in 1987.<ref>{{cite web | title=Alexander Givental - the Mathematics Genealogy Project | url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=32851 }}</ref> He emigrated to the United States in 1990.

==Mathematical work==
He provided the first proof of the [[Mirror symmetry (string theory)#History|mirror conjecture]] for [[Calabi–Yau manifold]]s that are complete intersections in toric ambient spaces, in particular for [[quintic equation|quintic]] [[hypersurface]]s in  '''P'''<sup>4</sup>.<ref>{{cite journal
 | first=Alexander
 | last=Givental
 | title=Equivariant Gromov – Witten Invariants
 | journal=Int. Math. Res. Not.
 | volume=1996
 | number=13
 | pages=613–663
 | year=1996
 | doi=10.1155/S1073792896000414
 | arxiv=alg-geom/9603021
 | s2cid=554844
 | doi-access=<!-- not free-->
 }}</ref> As an extracurricular activity, he translates Russian poetry into English<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://math.berkeley.edu/~giventh/verse/verse_index.html|title=Verse Translations from Russian|author=Alexander Givental, Elysee Wilson-Egolf|website=|date=|publisher=|language=en|access-date=September 9, 2020}}</ref> and publishes books, including his own translation of a textbook ({{interlanguage link|Элементарная геометрия (Киселёв)|ru}}) in geometry by [[Andrey Kiselyov]] and poetry of [[Marina Tsvetaeva]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sumizdat.org/|title=Elementary Geometry|author=Andrey Kiselyov|author-link=Andrey Kiselyov|website=|date=|publisher=Sumizdat|language=en|access-date=September 9, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite book
 |first=Marina |last=Tsvetaeva |editor1-first=Alexander |editor1-last=Givental |editor2-first=Elysee |editor2-last=Wilson-Egolf
 |title= To You – in 10 Decades
 |publisher= Sumizdat
 |year= 2013
 |pages         = 88
 |isbn          = 978-0977985272
}}</ref>

==Honours==
Givental was a speaker at the 1994 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Zurich.<ref>{{cite web | title=ICM Plenary & Invited Speakers &#124; International Congress of Mathematicians | url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=&order=field_section_speaker_type&sort=desc&page=108 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Givental is a father of two.
